title: Changing the customer reprices nothing and counts the tier lines
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses.
  • Have a new matrix for this test, matrix A, pricing a new category made for this test, category A, with one range from $0.00: Default Markup % 50, tier A Markup % 20.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, on tier A for work orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, on Default for work orders.
  • Have a new inventory part for this test, part F, in category A with a fixed sell price of $40.00.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, with four category A part lines: line 1 and line 2 at a cost of $10.00 (sold at $12.00), line 3 with a typed price of $14.00, and part F.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open work order 1's three-dot menu.
  3. Click Change Customer.
  4. Pick customer B.
  5. Click Update Customer.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu lists Change Customer, Split Work Order and Back to Work Orders.

Step 3:

  • The Change Customer dialog opens.

Step 4:

  • The amber note names Default for new work orders.

Step 5:

  • Lines 1 and 2 still sell at $12.00, line 3 at $14.00 and part F at $40.00.
  • A notice reads "2 lines priced at" tier A's name "for the previous customer" (4 lines − 1 Manual − 1 Fixed price = 2).
  • Lines 1 and 2 show no Manual icon; line 3 keeps its Manual icon.
